note: Planted errors for the claims canary and calibration suite (D21.1, AC-7.5). None restates misconceptions[]. Which job is which lives only in $PTK_STATE/claims-private/.

mutations.find: printf does not reinterpret the bits of a for %f. It receives the double that (double)a made.
mutations.replace: printf never changes the bits; the format string only decides how to read them, so %f reads a's own bits as a double.
mutations.why_false: With (double)a the argument is a new double 66.0 (6.3.1.4p2); printf receives that value, not a's int bits.

mutations.find: (unsigned)a converts 66 to unsigned int. 66 fits there, so the value stays 66
mutations.replace: (unsigned)a never changes a value, so the value stays 66
mutations.why_false: A negative int converted to unsigned int changes value (6.3.1.3p2); only representable values are unchanged.

mutations.find: %f prints a double with six digits after the decimal point when no precision is given
mutations.replace: %f prints a double with as many digits as it needs after the decimal point
mutations.why_false: A missing precision is taken as 6 (7.21.6.1p8).

sources.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 (C17), working draft N2176
sources.quote: If any argument is not the correct type for the corresponding conversion specification, the behavior is undefined.

mutations.why_false: The %c conversion is described in 7.21.6.1p8; paragraph 9 is about wrong argument types.
The behaviour is undefined (7.21.6.1p9); no output is guaranteed and ub.c is never run.

mutations.find: Its bits are 01000010, which is 0x42 in hex.
mutations.replace: Its bits are 01000010, which is 0x24 in hex.
